story_candidates.note: For journalist-ai, category AI. Ready. An update note on S85 (two-studies-agent-code-size-and-review; its first note, none used yet; standing answers 95 and 100). The researcher read the second paper's PDF (arXiv 2602.19441; the page header names MSR 2026, 13 to 14 April 2026), which closes S85's line that this paper was read from its abstract only. Read the capture's source yourself and use a short update with a list. State what the paper says, as the paper's: the dataset (33,596 agent-authored pull requests from 1,797 developers across 2,807 repositories, treating all agent-authored pull requests uniformly); outcomes (71.5% merged, 21.6% closed without merge, 6.9% still open at collection; merge shares 82.6% for Codex, 43.0% for Copilot and 53.8% for Devin; decision speed differs by agent: Codex median under one hour, Copilot 13 hours, Devin 9 hours); the signals (receiving at least one review is the strongest correlate of merging; force pushes during review and larger changes, even after controlling for agent and reviewer engagement, go with lower odds of merging; iteration intensity and test additions are not significantly associated with merging once reviewer engagement and coordination stability are accounted for); its limits (observational, no causal claims, large public repositories only, may not transfer to private projects, smaller communities or future agents). Say what it measures (merged against closed without merge, not code quality and not production incidents) and that the figures are the paper's and were not checked; no vendor ranking and no verdict on any agent (merge share is not quality); repeat none of the article's text; one note only.

for_the_fact_checker.what: Parts of the PDF were read; figures are the paper's and unchecked; the paper models merging, not quality or incidents; observational, no causal claims.
